definition: Dilatory means tending to delay; slow to act.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word dilatory. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know dilatory should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The landlord was notoriously dilatory about repairs: tenants learned that a promise of 'next week' meant a month if it meant anything.
Unhurried is neutral, even pleasant — a Sunday stroll is unhurried; it stops well short of dilatory, which blames the slowness for delaying something owed.
Obstructive goes further than dilatory: the dilatory party drags its feet, while the obstructive one actively blocks the road.

Tardy means late against a fixed time — the class bell, the 9 a.m. meeting — and it usually describes a single miss. Dilatory describes the habit behind repeated lateness: a settled tendency to delay that earns blame.
Sluggish means slow from low energy — cold syrup, a drained battery, a sleepy Monday crew — with no hint of intent. Dilatory carries fault: the dilatory party delays something owed, often on purpose.

Dawdling is wasting time in small, aimless ways — poking along, stopping to look at everything. It is childlike where dilatory is accusatory: courts call stalling tactics dilatory, but nobody files a formal complaint about dawdling.

Dilatory means tending to delay; slow to act.
The insurance company's dilatory handling of claims was strategy, not sloppiness — adjusters were coached to request one more document each week until exhausted claimants settled for less.

Dilatory is sharper than 'slow': slowness can be innocent, but dilatory behavior tends toward delay — often deliberately — and the word carries a note of blame, which is why courts and referees use it for stalling tactics.
Dilatory belongs to formal complaint — audits, rulings, referee reports — where slowness is a fault.
For a friend who is simply slow, 'poky' or 'slow' will do; say dilatory when the delay looks like a habit or a tactic and you mean to assign blame.
